executionHistory.summary: Running this packet's required E2E set exposed a second test-integrity defect, the mirror image of the false-green class this spec family keeps finding: a false RED. Four of five required tests failed on a cold stack in about 0.04s each with error_cause=assistant_http_not_ready and facade_invoked=false, which is not a dedup regression because the turn never reached the facade. /api/health returns 200 as soon as the core HTTP server listens, but the assistant facade wires asynchronously after the ML sidecar reports ready, so waitHTTPTurnHealthy alone lets a test fire into that gap; the one test that passed never posts a turn. Re-running could not have fixed it, because the stack is torn down after every run and every run is therefore a cold start. Fixed by wiring the EXISTING fail-loud helper waitAssistantFacadeReady, already used by two other specs, into the four affected tests. A t.Skipf on 503 would also have turned the lane green and would have been precisely the wrong fix, reproducing the pattern BUG-069-005 exists to remove; the chosen helper calls t.Fatalf on deadline so a genuine wiring failure still surfaces red. After the fix: five of five PASS, zero SKIP, exit 0. The dedup assertions now execute against a bound facade, which is what makes SameTransportMessageIDDedupes real evidence rather than an unreached assertion.

Verified the delivered implement phase as a specialist rather than re-implementing it, and corrected the phase claim from parent-expanded to specialist because a dispatch that returned no output is not a missing capability. Read internal/assistant/httpadapter/dedup.go directly: the cache key is turnDedupKey{userDigest, transport, messageID} where begin() hashes the user ID with sha256.Sum256 and pins transport to TransportName, so auth scoping is structural and a same-ID turn from another identity cannot collide. The lease carries owner bool; the first caller for a key executes and every later caller gets a non-owner lease whose wait() selects on entry.ready against ctx.Done(), so a duplicate blocks on the owner instead of re-executing yet still unblocks if its own client drops. complete() is owner-guarded and re-checks entry identity under the lock before stamping expiresAt and closing ready. Retention is bounded on both axes: removeExpiredLocked drops completed entries past TTL and evictOldestCompletedLocked walks the LRU list from the back and evicts only entries already marked completed, so an in-flight turn is never evicted out from under its waiters and a cache saturated with in-flight work refuses new unique work rather than corrupting a live lease. Read the adapter.go wiring: line 75 builds the cache from HTTPTurnDedupCapacity=16384 plus ConversationTTL and the injected clock; line 383 calls begin() with a sha256 fingerprint of the marshalled request, which is what converts a changed payload under a reused ID into 409 transport_message_id_conflict at line 385 instead of a silent second execution, with capacity exhaustion as 503 at line 388; the non-owner branch at line 396 replays cached status and body under a fresh Trace.RequestID and returns without reaching facade.Handle, while the owner branch invokes facade.Handle exactly once and completes on both outcomes, 500 at line 409 and 200 at line 428, so an accepted failure is replayed rather than retried. Confirmation run of ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run TestHTTPTurnDedup --verbose returned exit 0 with 8 RUN, 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, each PASS paired with its own === RUN line. The httpadapter ok line reports a real 0.083s duration and does NOT carry the [no tests to run] suffix, which is the discriminator against a vacuous pass and is meaningful rather than incidental because the same run emits that suffix 203 times for packages the selector correctly matches nothing in. The E2E suite was intentionally not re-executed because it takes a flock suite lock and the required set already carries a recorded green; that green was produced against exactly this tree, which was checked rather than assumed. git status --porcelain carries three modified source paths, tests/e2e/assistant/transport_hint_parity_test.go, web_pwa_chat_e2e_test.go and web_pwa_retry_e2e_test.go, whose diff is precisely the four added waitAssistantFacadeReady calls of that same false-RED fix, with mtimes at 19:24Z predating this phase at 19:44Z. Everything this phase wrote is packet artifacts.

The three survivors are correct survivors because none touches the disabled branch; killing all eight would have been the weaker outcome since it would mean the suite cannot separate the replay path from cache bookkeeping.
